plans.note: Section 21 is the operative cap. 21.1 is mutual, greater of 12-month fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; 21.2 excludes consequentials but preserves data restoration/replacement costs as direct; 21.3 defines Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, IP infringement); 21.4 preserves independence of caps. Check the cap against insurance limits in 18.1 and the indemnity gap under INDEMN before scoring.

No Section 20 appears in the outline even though 9.3 cross-references 'the remedies required by Section 20.5' and 21.3 carves out 'indemnification obligations' and 30.5 references an 'indemnified party'. Treat as a missing Vendor indemnity (IP infringement plus data/security and unlawful conduct) unless a Section 20 exists outside the supplied outline; confirm before scoring missing.

sec-12.4-2 imposes a 24-month, all-territory, all-product non-compete on Customer — squarely prohibited by this rule. Note the direct conflict with sec-12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete commitment; use that inconsistency in the rationale.

sec-12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to engage any supplier (favourable). The de facto constraint sits in sec-7.2 (disclose-and-match before engaging another provider) and the take-or-pay in sec-2.1; assess whether that match right operates as exclusivity, but avoid double-flagging the same term already handled under MFN and MINCOMMIT.

The first sec-7.2 (there are two clauses numbered 7.2) requires Customer to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers — an MFN running against us, the wrong direction under this rule. sec-12.3 disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment and evidences the inconsistency.

sec-12.4 bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out and unlimited employee scope. Contrast sec-12.3, which preserves hiring anyone responding to general recruitment.

Section 9 contains only cause-based, insolvency, security/SLA and force-majeure exits (9.1–9.3, 9.5, 27.3); no termination for convenience appears, and sec-2.1 affirmatively removes reduction or termination rights. Note there is no Section 9.4 in the outline — check whether a convenience right was dropped.

sec-8.2 gives 30-day non-renewal notice with a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if the reminder is missed; sec-8.3 caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Both look at or above the preferred position — confirm before proposing anything.

Direct conflict: sec-28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction (outside the accepted list), while sec-28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. Resolve to an accepted law/venue pair; sec-28.3 is an escalation step that preserves urgent relief.

sec-24.1 permits Customer affiliate/successor assignment without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and delegation; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. Cross-check sec-13.3 (licence transfer keyed to Section 24). Direction favours us.

sec-14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP, but sec-14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence back — the core deviation. Read with sec-1.4 (Deliverable), sec-14.3 (Vendor Technology and the 13.2 perpetual licence) and sec-15.1 (no training/model use of Customer Data).

sec-13.1 extends access to Affiliates and contractors; sec-13.2 gives a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology; sec-13.3 limits revocation/suspension to uncured material breach after notice. The revocability problem is confined to the Deliverable licence in sec-14.2 — coordinate with the IP rule so the same term is not flagged twice.

sec-22.1 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, via an independent auditor; sec-22.2 puts costs on Vendor absent a 5% underpayment and bars system/data access; sec-22.3 makes findings our Confidential Information. Section 23 (records/assurance) has no text supplied — check it does not add a broader audit right.

No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination-fee clause appears against Customer; sec-7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately not due. The nearest economic penalty is the sec-2.1 take-or-pay, which belongs under MINCOMMIT — do not double-flag.

sec-19.1–19.3 give services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, full subscription term for hosted Services), malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties; sec-19.4 provides repair/re-perform then termination and refund, expressly non-exclusive for indemnified and security claims; sec-19.5 is a limited disclaimer that preserves express warranties. Acceptance remedies in Section 6 are the related mechanic.

sec-18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; sec-18.2 adds certificates, primacy and a statement that insurance does not limit liability. Verify cyber limits are adequate given the hosted health-data profile, but the clause exists.

sec-2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay for three years expressly 'without reduction or termination rights' — no exit, which is the walk-away trigger for this rule. Note the conflict with sec-12.3 (no minimum-volume commitment) and the absence of any convenience termination in Section 9.

sec-10.1 assumes an 'agreed transition period' and sec-10.2 covers Deliverable delivery and refunds, but neither obligates Vendor to return or export Customer Data in a usable format or to provide exit assistance. sec-16.5 defers Customer Data to 'Sections 11 and 15', and Section 11 is absent from the outline — confirm whether the data-return mechanics exist before scoring.
